items.title: Why Electricity Travels at High Voltage ⚡ Power Grid Explained #Shorts

ai.summary: Based on the title metadata, the short video explains why power is transmitted at high voltage: raising voltage reduces current for a given power level, which cuts resistive (I²R) losses and improves long‑distance transmission efficiency. It likely also notes the need for transformers to step voltages up and down and the associated insulation and safety considerations.
bullets: Higher voltage lowers current for the same power, reducing I²R (resistive) losses on lines.
Lower current lets operators use smaller conductors or carry more power on the same conductor size.
Transformers are required to step voltage up for transmission and down for distribution/loads.
Higher voltages demand greater insulation, clearances, and substation/tower design considerations.
High‑voltage transmission is a primary tool for efficient long‑distance power delivery.
takeaways: Line voltage selection directly affects conductor sizing, capital cost, and transmission losses — key for route and budget decisions.
Transformer siting and rating are central to stepping voltages; substation design must balance efficiency and O&M constraints.
Insulation, clearance, and right‑of‑way requirements grow with voltage and materially impact tower and civil design.
Understanding voltage‑loss tradeoffs is essential when integrating remote generation or planning long‑haul transmission links.
